clue.text: 15's dip to seize prey, wings torn off

explanation.surface: A bird of prey swoops into the water to seize its catch, losing its wings.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 is the band at 15-across, so '15's' defines one of their songs; 'wings torn off' strips the outer letters of prey.
explanation.definitionFit: Breathe is a track on Pink Floyd's album The Dark Side of the Moon.

clue.text: See 18
Time saved by unscrambling of a Gemini crossword, primarily cryptic

the letters of a Gemini are sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: A star-sign Gemini saves time by solving a crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unscrambling of' turns A GEMINI into ENIGMAI; T goes in before the final I, then C ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cryptic is puzzling and obscure in meaning, just as an enigmatic remark is.

clue.text: Name tag's initial, lining hat

indicators.note: the initial letter forms a lining inside the hat word

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat

indicators.note: initial means the first letter of tag's

explanation.walkthrough: TILE is dated British slang for a hat; T from tag goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is the name of a book, film or song, or a person's honorific name.

clue.text: English city Paul built for Australian natives

indicators.note: built suggests the letters are put together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The setter Paul constructs an English city in honour of native Australians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'built' rearranges CITY PAUL to UCALYPTI. Paul is the setter's own pseudonym, making the surface self-referential.
explanation.definitionFit: Eucalyptus trees, gum trees, are native to Australia; this is the Latin plural.

clue.text: Pleased to see hit involving heroes, for a start

indicators.note: involving means the struck word wraps around the heroes' start

explanation.surface: Someone is delighted to watch heroes landing a blow.
explanation.walkthrough: CHUFFED is British slang for delighted.
explanation.definitionFit: Chuffed is informal British slang for delighted or very satisfied.

clue.text: See 23
Discouraging classic hit breaking farmers in middle of July

the Beatles title breaks into the farmers' union letters

Help! is a classic Beatles hit single

explanation.surface: An old pop hit put off farmers in midsummer.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Farmers' Union is Britain's farmers' trade body; 'breaking' puts the Beatles hit inside it, and 'middle of July' drops J and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unhelpful, giving no assistance, is discouraging to someone trying to get something done.

clue.text: One intercepting newspaper feature

indicators.note: the one word cuts in between the newspaper's letters

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper
an ace is one in cards or dice

explanation.surface: Someone intercepts a newspaper's feature article.
explanation.definitionFit: A facet is one aspect or feature of something, like a face of a cut gem.

clue.text: See 23
Old dictator, Pol's partner, executed the divvy

parts.note: Idi Amin was the dictator of Uganda

indicators.note: executed means beheaded, losing the first letter

parts.note: Pol Pot, the Cambodian dictator, has Pot as partner to Pol

explanation.surface: Two old dictators named, one of them put to death by the fool.
explanation.walkthrough: IDI Amin and Pol POT; executing POT takes its head, leaving OT. 'Divvy' is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Divvy is British slang for a stupid person, a fool.

clue.text: Dance tease, say

parts.note: tease sounds like teas, and cha is slang for tea
the second of the teas, again cha
the third of the teas, again cha

explanation.walkthrough: 'say' asks you to hear 'tease' as 'teas'; CHA is British slang for tea, so several teas give CHA three times.
explanation.definitionFit: The cha-cha-cha is a Latin American ballroom dance.

clue.text: Capitals of Italy, Morocco and Germany less popular in important 8 city?

indicators.note: the capitals and trimmed city go inside the important word

in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A list of capital cities, with Germany's falling out of fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is DIAMOND; Kimberley in South Africa is famous for diamond mining. Germany's capital BERLIN minus IN leaves BERL.
explanation.definitionFit: Kimberley in South Africa grew up around diamond mines, including the Big Hole.

clue.text: Game tease, say, in John

indicators.note: the two letters sit inside the toilet word

parts.note: john and loo are both slang for a toilet

explanation.walkthrough: 'tease' heard aloud is 'Ts', two Ts, placed inside LOO; 'John' is US slang and 'loo' British slang for toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a game of chance in which numbers are drawn, like bingo or a lottery.

clue.text: Regarding the birth of the bum

definitions.meaning: relating to birth, as in prenatal care
relating to the buttocks, from nates, the anatomical term for them

explanation.definitionFit: Natal means relating to birth, and also, from nates, relating to the buttocks.

clue.text: Rearing meat, you waste sugar

to lose is to waste

explanation.surface: Someone raising calves for meat tells you it wastes sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rearing' turns VEAL into LAEV.
explanation.definitionFit: Laevulose is another name for fructose, the sugar found in fruit and honey.

clue.text: Old chef's after salmon for group

indicators.note: after places the chef's name following the colour

parts.note: salmon is a shade of pink
Keith Floyd was a flamboyant British TV chef who died in 2009

explanation.surface: A dead chef's recipe comes after the salmon course for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: Keith FLOYD was a well-known British television cook.
explanation.definitionFit: Pink Floyd is a British rock band, the theme of this puzzle.

clue.text: "Numbers" originally called "number" in error, raised

indicators.note: raised means the whole piece reads upwards in this down clue
the birth name and figure go inside the error word

nee, French for born, marks a woman's original name
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A list called Numbers was wrongly titled number, and somebody objected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally called' is the née of a woman's maiden name; 'raised' turns the whole assembly to read upwards, not just the error word.
explanation.definitionFit: Nineteens are numbers, plural instances of the number nineteen.

clue.text: Wild dog taking drink, head down

indicators.note: the first letter, the head, is sent down to the bottom of this down entry

parts.note: the corgi is a Welsh breed of dog
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: A wild dog laps up a drink with its head lowered.
explanation.walkthrough: CORGI then ASTI gives CORGIASTI; 'head down' moves its first letter C to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Orgiastic means unrestrained and frenzied, like a wild party.

clue.text: Growth in ecstasy through distribution of narcotic

explanation.walkthrough: 'distribution of' rearranges the narcotic letters, and 'through' threads the drug letter between them; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Accretion is gradual growth by the build-up of added layers.

clue.text: 15's doctor went into a hall to pen "Two Little Boys"

indicators.note: to pen means to enclose, so the boys' names are shut inside
to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are rearranged

Herb and Rick are short, little forms of the boys' names Herbert and Richard

explanation.surface: A doctor walks into a hall to write the old song Two Little Boys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' rearranges WENT INTO A HALL to ANOT...INTHEWALL, which pens HERB and RICK. Two Little Boys is a Rolf Harris song, a misleading musical title.
explanation.definitionFit: Another Brick in the Wall is a Pink Floyd song from the album The Wall.

clue.text: Escape that's authorised, in a word?

definitions.meaning: British slang for to run away
written as a single word, the phrase becomes slang for lawful

clue.text: Like jelly? 4, perhaps, for triangular plate

four is a square number, two times two

explanation.walkthrough: '4' looks like a cross-reference to 4-down; it is simply the number four.
explanation.definitionFit: A set square is a flat triangular drawing instrument used to draw angles.

clue.text: 15's timid about one gaseous element, shifting my zodiac around

clue.text: Line in letter recited

explanation.walkthrough: 8 is DIAMOND (slang 'rock') and 7 is FACET ('side'); HIDE ROCK SIDE said aloud gives the chemical word.

clue.text: Right pair of OT characters, free

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Old Testament book of Samuel
Eve is the first woman in Genesis, in the Old Testament
